chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says, 'God knows what He did not know,' the Throne shakes in magnification for Him.

key_terms.إِعْظَاماً: magnification/glorification — the Throne's shaking is an act of reverence, not distress
key_terms.اهْتَزَّ الْعَرْشُ: the Throne shakes — a Quranic/cosmological image expressing divine response to a profound event
key_terms.عَلِمَ اللَّهُ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمِ: God knows what He did not know — a theologically erroneous statement implying God's knowledge increases or changes

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about claiming God's knowledge increases or changes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against attributing ignorance to God, teaching that such a statement is so grave that it causes the Divine Throne to shake in awe. This hadith belongs to the theological chapters on Divine Knowledge (al-'Ilm) in al-Kafi, directed at Imam al-Sadiq's students who had to refute theological deviants — particularly those who attributed change or acquisition of new knowledge to God. The original audience would understand 'the Throne shaking' as a cosmic sign of divine displeasure, rooted in the Quranic image of the Throne bearing witness to God's majesty.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Wahab Bin Hafs, from Abu 
Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who says, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Knower’, what he does not know, the Throne shakes in Magnification for Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Wahab ibn Hafs who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one says, “Allah has the knowledge”, when he does not know something, the Throne of Allah vibrates as a sign of expressing His greatness.’”
